subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 6
summary: RBL Bank Play tweaks its welcome benefit window, Standard Chartered adds a renewal fee waiver, ICICI's Times Black gets a bigger lounge network, and two Axis Bank Purchase cards swap concierge for golf.
body_html:
Today's a mixed bag, and that's honestly the most common kind of day in this newsletter. One card got a genuinely better deal, one got a clearer fee waiver, one got a lounge upgrade, and two business cards traded a benefit you'd probably never use for one you actually might. Let's go issuer by issuer.

RBL Bank Play Credit Card

The welcome benefit window changed from a flat "3 months" after you get the card to "60 days after your first statement is generated."

Here's why this isn't as simple as it sounds. Your first statement usually lands about 30 days after you start using the card, so 60 days after that puts you at roughly 90 days from activation, close to where the old 3-month window landed anyway. If your first billing cycle runs long for any reason, this new rule could actually give you a little more runway. If it runs short, you get a little less.

The catch: don't assume this is neutral. Check your card's actual statement date, then count 60 days from there, and use that as your real deadline for hitting whatever spend or activity earns the welcome benefit. Don't go by "3 months from when I got the card" anymore, that math no longer applies.

Standard Chartered Super Value Titanium Credit Card

Good news on this one: the renewal fee is now waived if you spent ₹90,000 or more in the preceding year. Standard Chartered also added a clearer Eligibility & Documents section to the card page, which is a readability fix, not a benefit change.

Do the math on whether ₹90,000 a year is realistic for you: that's ₹7,500 a month, which is well within reach if you're using this as your fuel and daily-spend card, which is what it's positioned for. Cross that line and your renewal fee, typically in the ₹500 to ₹750 range on cards in this tier, is reversed automatically.

The catch: you need to hit ₹90,000 in the year *before* your renewal, not the year after. If you're a light spender who mostly keeps this card for the fuel surcharge waiver and doesn't otherwise put much through it, you'll likely still pay the renewal fee.

ICICI Bank Times Black Credit Card

Straightforward upgrade: domestic and international lounge access went from "1,400+ lounges in 145+ countries" to "1,900+ lounges in 145+ countries." Same country coverage, meaningfully more lounges to actually walk into.

The catch: more lounges in the network doesn't automatically mean more free visits for you. Your card's per-quarter or per-year visit cap and any spend threshold to unlock it haven't changed here, only the size of the network you can use those visits in. Check your existing visit limit before assuming this means unlimited lounge-hopping.

Axis Bank Purchase Card

This corporate card swapped its 24x7 Concierge Services benefit for a 24x7 Golf benefit.

The catch: if you were actually using the concierge line, for travel bookings, reservations, that kind of thing, that's gone now. If you golf, this is a straight upgrade. If you do neither, this changes nothing for you either way.

Axis Bank Purchase Control (Virtual Card)

Same trade as the Purchase Card above: 24x7 Concierge Services out, 24x7 Golf benefit in. Axis also tidied up the page by removing a "Got more questions? Locate the nearest branch" section, which is a page cleanup, not a benefit change.

The catch: identical to the Purchase Card above, this only matters to you if you actually used the concierge service or would use the golf benefit.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold the RBL Bank Play Credit Card, go find your actual first statement date and count 60 days from it, don't rely on the old "3 months" rule of thumb anymore.

If you hold the Standard Chartered Super Value Titanium, check your last 12 months of spend on the card. If you're anywhere near ₹90,000, you're probably clearing it already and this renewal fee waiver is free money you weren't expecting.

If you hold the ICICI Times Black, this is a pure upgrade with no catch worth worrying about, nothing to do here except enjoy the bigger network.

If you hold either Axis Bank Purchase Card variant, this only changes anything for you if concierge or golf were ever part of why you kept the card. For most cardholders, this one's a non-event.

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you make a call on any of this, run it past a professional or at least sleep on it. But this is exactly how I'd think about it if these were my cards.

Monzy
